import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Identify potential drivers based on mean_y1-mean_y0 difference
    diffs = [abs(feats.y[feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)] > 0].mean() - 
                feats.y[feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)] <= 0].mean()) 
             for fid in feats.ids]
    
    # Sort by effect size
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(diffs)[::-1]
    
    # Filter out near-duplicates (correlated features)
    kept_ids = []
    correlated_pairs = set()
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        if feats.ids[i] in correlated_pairs:
            continue
        kept_ids.append(feats.ids[i])
        # Add all correlated features to the exclusion set
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if feats.ids[j] in correlated_pairs:
                continue
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(feats.ids[i])], 
                              feats.x[:, feats.column(feats.ids[j])])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                correlated_pairs.add(feats.ids[j])
    
    # Select top drivers
    drivers = tuple(kept_ids[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # Build columns and products
    columns = list(kept_ids[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    products = []
    
    # Add interaction terms for top features
    for i in range(len(columns)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(columns)):
            products.append((columns[i], columns[j]))
    
    # Create weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for fid in columns:
        loadings[fid] = diffs[sorted_indices.tolist().index(feats.ids.index(fid))]
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=tuple(columns), products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
